name: Megan Thee Stallion
description:
'''Megan Jovon Ruth Pete''' (born February 15, 1995), known professionally as '''Megan Thee Stallion''',{{efn|Pronounced "the", not "[[thee]]". Specifically, she pronounces the "Thee" as an unstressed {{IPAc-en|ð|ə}}, and not {{IPAc-en|ð|iː}} as in "[[thee]]" or a stressed "the".<ref>{{cite web|title = Megan Thee Stallion's ABCs|via = [[YouTube]]| date=July 9, 2019 |url-status = live |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190727220004/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0DxH8RGNKDY|archive-date = July 27, 2019|url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0DxH8RGNKDY|access-date = July 29, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title = Megan Thee Stallion Sings Rihanna, Beyoncé and Khalid in a Game of Song Association| via = [[YouTube]]| date = June 27, 2019| url-status = live | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190715160018/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aBR7676_Rr4| archive-date = July 15, 2019| url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=aBR7676_Rr4| access-date = July 29, 2019}}</ref>}} is an American rapper, songwriter, and actress. She gained recognition after videos of her [[freestyling]] went viral on [[social media]]. After signing [[1501 Certified Entertainment]], she released her debut mixtape [[Fever (mixtape)|''Fever'']] (2019) and the [[extended play]] ''[[Suga (EP)|Suga]]'' (2020), both of which reached the top ten of the [[Billboard 200|''Billboard'' 200]]. She achieved mainstream success with the singles "[[Cash Shit]]", "[[Hot Girl Summer]]", and "[[Savage (Megan Thee Stallion song)|Savage]]".

Megan's debut studio album, [[Good News (Megan Thee Stallion album)|''Good News'']] (2020), included a [[Savage (Megan Thee Stallion song)#Beyoncé remix|remix]] of "Savage" featuring [[Beyoncé]], which topped the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] and won two [[Grammy Awards]]. In 2021, she featured on [[Cardi B]]'s single "[[WAP (song)|WAP]]", which became her second US number-one single. Her next studio albums, ''[[Traumazine]]'' (2022) and [[Megan (album)|''Megan'']] (2024), were influenced by a lawsuit with her former label. The latter's second single, "[[Hiss (song)|Hiss]]", became her first solo number-one single on the ''Billboard'' Hot 100 and made her the first solo female rapper to debut at number one on the [[Billboard Global 200|''Billboard'' Global 200]].

Megan is the recipient of [[List of awards and nominations received by Megan Thee Stallion|various accolades]], including six [[BET Awards]], five [[BET Hip Hop Awards]], four [[American Music Awards]], four [[MTV Video Music Awards]], a [[Billboard Women in Music|''Billboard'' Women in Music Award]], and three [[Grammy Awards]]. At the [[63rd Annual Grammy Awards]], she became the second female rapper to win [[Grammy Award for Best New Artist|Best New Artist]], after [[Lauryn Hill]] in [[41st Annual Grammy Awards|1999]]. [[Time (magazine)|''Time'']] named her one of the [[Time 100|100 most influential people in the world]] in 2020. She has also pursued acting, including starring in the [[Moulin Rouge! (musical)#Broadway (2019–2026)|2026 Broadway production of ''Moulin Rouge! The Musical'']] and the documentary ''[[Megan Thee Stallion: In Her Words]]'' (2024).
